title: Intrinsic kinetic graph Poincare stress for Q3 likelihood rows
question: Can the R-399 conditional shell use the Hamiltonian kinetic carré-du-champ directly, by replacing the unstable coordinate nearest-neighbour comparison with the intrinsic Poincare gap of its momentum-weighted graph?

new_perspective.principle: Use the actual kinetic form as the conditional Dirichlet form, rather than forcing it through a cutoff-sensitive coordinate spacing comparison.
route: For each conditional law pi, build the symmetric graph conductance c_ij=(pi_i+pi_j)|p_ij|^2/(2 chi) in the q basis.
Compute the smallest positive eigenvalue of the pi-weighted graph Laplacian and test E_kin(f)>=gap*Var_pi(f) on every actual likelihood row.
Repeat all R-403 cutoff, beta, source, history, order, prefix, adjoint and orientation contexts, while reporting the intrinsic gap profile separately from the coordinate form.

Use the p-to-q mutation as a structural hostile test: q is diagonal in the q basis and therefore has zero conductance, whereas the genuine momentum graph is connected on the finite oscillator fixture.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: If an analytic lower bound for this intrinsic gap can be proved on a cutoff-independent Hamiltonian core, the R-399 shell transfer may avoid the divergent E_kin/D_q upper comparison. The finite graph gap itself is not a common-core, phase, continuum or QFT theorem.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar nonnegativity and finite scope arithmetic; the graph Laplacian eigenvalues, matrix rows and all cutoff/phase/volume limits remain in the executable/open boundary.

promotion_criteria: Prove a cutoff-independent lower bound for the momentum-weighted graph gap on a Hamiltonian common core, not just a finite eigenvalue profile.
Control source, phase, volume, orientation and exhaustion dependence and identify the intrinsic form with the required shell observable.
Only after those analytic controls may the intrinsic form replace the R-399 coordinate Dirichlet form in a regulator limit.
stop_conditions: If the intrinsic graph gap collapses with cutoff, do not replace D_q by E_kin in the shell transfer.
If the graph is disconnected or the likelihood variance is not controlled, retain this as a finite diagnostic only.
Finite positivity of a weighted graph gap is not a common-core, phase-uniform or QFT theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite intrinsic kinetic graph stress. It proves no cutoff-independent or volume-independent gap, no common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The intrinsic graph route removes the unstable coordinate upper-comparison step only at the finite diagnostic level; it does not supply the analytic uniform lower bound required for promotion.
